title: Trajectory sharpening under quantum reference frame transformations
abstract: Quantum reference frame (QRF) transformations relate the description of a physical system to different quantum observers, but their connection to concrete experimental phenomena remains largely unclear. Here we show that the trajectory-sharpening effect obtained by correlating a probed system with an effective negative-mass reference admits a natural interpretation as a QRF transformation to the frame of a negative-mass system. Using a minimal toy model of free particles with signed masses, we identify the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-type observables responsible for this effect with a pair of commuting relational observables that, under the instantaneous QRF transformation, are mapped to operators local to distinct subsystems. We then show that the corresponding relational trajectory is reproduced by the dynamical QRF transformation, where the transformed relational position acquires an explicit time dependence. We introduce QRF-invariant sharpness measures for relational trajectories and derive monogamy relations showing that a trajectory cannot be made simultaneously arbitrarily sharp with respect to two distinct negative-mass frames. We further show that trajectory sharpness can instead reside in a collective reference mode encoded across two physical systems, even when neither constituent alone provides an arbitrarily sharp reference, so that sharpness can be distributed rather than localized in a single constituent frame. These results provide an operational, experimentally relevant interpretation of QRF transformations for continuous-variable systems.
summary: This paper connects the abstract concept of Quantum Reference Frame transformations to measurable physical effects, specifically trajectory sharpening. Using toy models with negative masses, the authors show that this sharpening is mathematically equivalent to a QRF transformation. The key finding is that sharpness can be distributed across multiple coupled systems rather than being confined to a single reference frame.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide an operational, experimentally relevant interpretation of abstract Quantum Reference Frame (QRF) transformations, particularly concerning trajectory sharpening.
main_result: It shows that trajectory sharpening relative to a negative-mass reference frame is equivalent to a QRF transformation, and it derives monogamy relations showing sharpness can be distributed across collective modes rather than localized in a single frame.
method: The analysis uses minimal toy models of free particles with signed masses, developing QRF-invariant sharpness measures and analyzing the transformation of observables under both kinematical and dynamical QRF transformations.
model_or_system: The model involves multiple quantum systems (A, B, C) whose dynamics are analyzed using free Hamiltonians. The core mathematical tool is the QRF transformation operator, which is extended to handle effective negative masses.
key_observables: Trajectory sharpness measures (marginal uncertainty product, covariance-area measure), and commuting relational observables (EPR-type observables).
important_parameters: Effective negative mass ($m_A = -m$), the mass ratio $\lambda_{CA} = |m_C/m_A|$, and the time dependence of the transformation $\hat{S}_T(t)$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption of block-diagonal covariance between internal and collective modes, and the initial justification of negative mass systems via experimental contexts like atomic spin ensembles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transformation process, showing position uncertainty in different frames and demonstrating how relative trajectory sharpness can be achieved via the negative-mass reference system.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical problem (QRF interpretation) to developing the mathematical machinery (QRF transformations, handling negative masses) and finally applying this to derive quantitative results regarding the distribution and limits of trajectory sharpness.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, measurable framework for understanding how reference frames affect quantum measurements, which is crucial for interpreting results in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.
